That's the word, friend. The LORD says He has consecrated the temple “by putting My Name there forever.” Then He adds that His eyes and His heart will be there for all time. Forever and all time in the same breath. That's a promise with no end date on it.

A lifetime is a long stretch, friend, and I wish my sprinkles lasted one. But the LORD says more than that. He has consecrated the temple “by putting My Name there forever.” The word is forever, and it's right there in verse 3.

Seventy years has a nice round ring to it, but it isn't in this passage. The LORD says He put His Name in the temple “forever.” He also says His eyes and His heart will be there for all time. No countdown timer here, friend.

Yes, friend. The LORD says to walk before Him “as your father David walked.” David was Israel's king before Solomon, and Solomon's father. The LORD describes that walk as one with a heart of integrity and uprightness.

Moses was Israel's leader who brought them out of Egypt, and a big name for sure. But God doesn't point to him here. He says to walk “as your father David walked.” The comparison is to Solomon's own dad, David, Israel's earlier king.

Joshua was the one who stepped up after Moses died (Joshua 1:1). Good name, friend, but not the one in this verse. The LORD says to walk before Him “as your father David walked.” It's Solomon's own father, David, who is held up here.

Throne it is, friend. God says that if Solomon walks as his father David walked, “then I will establish your royal throne over Israel forever.” That's the seat of the king. And look at the word again: forever.

An army sounds mighty, friend, but God doesn't say it here. He says He will establish Solomon's royal throne over Israel forever. The promise is about the king's seat, not the soldiers. Nobody in this verse is marching anywhere.

I can see why a treasury came to mind, friend. Solomon built a lot. But the verse says God will establish “your royal throne over Israel forever.” The promise is about the throne, not what's stored in a vault.

explanations.answer: Going off to serve other gods
explanations.explanation: That's the one, friend. The LORD says that if Solomon or his sons turn away, “and if you go off to serve and worship other gods,” then trouble follows. Turning away from God's commandments and going off to other gods are named together. It's the heart of the warning.

explanations.answer: Moving the ark out of the temple
explanations.explanation: Good thinking about the ark, friend, but God doesn't name it in this warning. He says that if they turn away, “and if you go off to serve and worship other gods.” That's the thing He points to here. Serving other gods is the answer.

explanations.answer: Building a bigger palace for himself
explanations.explanation: The palace comes up in verse 1, because Solomon had finished it. But God doesn't warn about a bigger palace. He says, “and if you go off to serve and worship other gods.” Other gods are what He names, friend.

explanations.answer: Why has the LORD done this
explanations.explanation: That's the question, friend. Those who pass by ask, “Why has the LORD done such a thing to this land and to this temple?” I think this one hurts a little. It's a sad picture, and the next verse gives an answer.

explanations.answer: Who will build it back up
explanations.explanation: That sounds like a hopeful question, friend. But it isn't the one they ask. Those passing by say, “Why has the LORD done such a thing to this land and to this temple?” I think this part of the passage is heavy.

explanations.answer: Where did all the gold go
explanations.explanation: Gold doesn't come up in what they ask, friend. Those passing by say, “Why has the LORD done such a thing to this land and to this temple?” They want to know why it happened. I think this is one of the heavy lines in the passage.

Egypt, friend. Verse 9 says Israel forsook “the LORD their God who brought their fathers out of the land of Egypt.” It reminds them who He is and what He did. It's right there in the answer people give.
Moab is a good guess, friend, but it's not in this verse. The text says the LORD “brought their fathers out of the land of Egypt.” Egypt is the land named.
Edom isn't named in this verse, friend. The text says the LORD “brought their fathers out of the land of Egypt.” That's the place God brought them out of. Egypt is the one.
